claim.pdf_says: 14.6.13.1.4 item 3): '... If execution of the declarative completes normally, execution continues as specified in the statement for normal execution. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is not executed.'
claim.markdown_says: '... If execution of the declarative completes normally, execution continues as specified in the rules for normal execution. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is not executed.'
claim.why_it_matters: Altered wording in a normative general rule: the standard points at 'the statement' (the interrupted statement itself), the transcription at 'the rules'. The practical effect is the same, but the transcription is no longer quotable verbatim as ISO text, and rule 1 of this project requires citing the spec exactly.

verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation on every available ground and all of them failed. (1) Not a reflow/wrapping artifact: the disputed word sits mid-line, not at a line break. In the 300 dpi render of printed page 550 (PDF page 580), item 3) of 14.6.13.1.4 wraps as 'hierarchy, the associated declarative is executed. If execution of the declarative completes normally, / execution continues as specified in the statement for normal execution. If a conditional phrase with / a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is / not executed.' A 2x LANCZOS magnification of that band (E:/Temp/specrecon/v580/crop_item3.png) renders the glyphs unambiguously: s-t-a-t-e-m-e-n-t. There is no hyphenation, no adjacent-line alternative, and no second occurrence of the phrase on the page that the transcriber could have been tracking. (2) The 'missing' text is genuinely absent, not present elsewhere: grep over specs/ISO_COBOL.md for 'as specified in the (rules|statement) for normal execution' returns exactly one hit, line 24248, and that hit reads 'rules'. The word 'statement' appears nowhere in that slot. (3) The claim misquotes neither source: both quoted strings are verbatim-correct against the render and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24248 respectively; the surrounding sentence, including the trailing NOT-phrase sentence, matches character for character in both. (4) The work-unit markdown is not an extraction artifact: the same 'rules' wording was confirmed directly in the checked-in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, so the defect is in the canonical transcription, not in page_workunit.py's slicing. Severity 'cosmetic' is correctly assigned: both readings direct the implementor to the same place (how the statement proceeds under normal execution), so no compiler behavior turns on the substitution. The likely mechanism is transcriber normalization toward the sibling phrasing: items 1), 2) and 4) of the very same list all read 'as specified in the rules for ...' ('the rules for the specific statement', 'the rules for the PERFORM statement', 'the rules for that statement'), so item 3)'s outlier 'the statement' — arguably an ISO drafting inconsistency in its own right — was silently regularized to match its neighbors. That regularization is exactly what makes the line unquotable verbatim.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim confirmed as stated; only two refinements. (a) Location: page 580 of the PDF is printed page 550; the text is 14.6.13.1.4 'Nonfatal exception conditions', numbered item 3), and the affected line in the transcription is specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24248. (b) Mechanism and framing: the substitution is not a random OCR slip but a normalization toward the sibling items — 1), 2) and 4) of the same list all read 'as specified in the rules for ...', while item 3) alone prints 'as specified in the statement for normal execution'. ISO's outlier wording ('the statement', arguably a drafting inconsistency on ISO's part) was regularized away. The characterization that the standard 'points at the interrupted statement itself' is an interpretation, not something the printed text says; the printed text merely reads 'the statement'. Fix: restore 'the statement' in item 3) of 14.6.13.1.4 and, if the reconciliation ledger tracks ISO's own defects, note the outlier so it is not re-normalized by a future pass.
